newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurdish group says it still backs ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurdish group says it still backs ceasefire.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish group said on Tuesday that it still supported the ceasefire with its rival in northern Iraq but reiterated it would not continue talks until the killing of one of its members was investigated.

"We emphasize that we are still committed to the peace process in Iraqi Kurdistan and to the ceasefire, as well as to all necessary measures for the consolidation of the ceasefire...," a statement from the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) said.

But the KDP, which last week walked out of talks with rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), reiterated that it would not go back to the Western-sponsored negotiations until the murder of one of its local leaders was investigated.
The two Kurdish groups control different parts of northern Iraq, which has effectively been out of Baghdad's control since the 1991 Gulf War.
"The KDP cannot attend any high level meetings until the terrorist acts against our members and premises are investigated," the statement said.
The KDP delegation at the Ankara talks accused the PUK of the attack on the KDP head in Halbja. The PUK denied any responsibility.
The two groups have met frequently in Ankara since they declared a ceasefire at the end of October after weeks of fighting. The talks were sponsored by the United States, Turkey and Britain.
The KDP used Iraqi troops and tanks to take the key city of Arbil from the PUK last August. The U.S. fired missiles at southern Iraq in response to Iraq's involvement.
